newsitem.title: LEBANON: Lebanese t-bill rates "acceptable"- cen bank chief.
newsitem.headline: Lebanese t-bill rates "acceptable"- cen bank chief.

text.p: Bank of Lebanon Governor Riad Salameh said in remarks on Wednesday that rates on Lebanese pound-denominated t-bills have reached acceptable levels, adding they would continue to fall but the decline would be limited.
"The levels which treasury bill rates reached are acceptable," Salameh said in remarks published by Beirut newspapers.

"The rates on most maturities have retreated, especially the two-year maturity which reached about 16.5 percent. These rates will not retreat except within narrow margins in order to create stability at the current levels," Salameh added.
The central bank, Bank of Lebanon, has since November reduced rates for its weekly t-bill issues at slightly faster rate than in earlier months.

Three-month bill yields for the February 6 issue fell to 13.96 percent from last week's 14.08. Yields for the six-month, one-year and two-year issues fell to 14.98, 15.37 and 16.34 percent respectively from 15.56, 15.84 and 17.14 percent.
